question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $56u + 24v = \text{gcd}(56,24).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}56 & = & \color{red}24\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}8 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}24 & = & \color{blue}8\cdot 3 & + & \color{blue}0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(56,24) =8.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}8 &= \color{red} 56 - 24\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 56 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{1} + 24 \cdot ( \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-2}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=1$ and $v=-2.$

Finally, \[u+v=1+(-2)=-1. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $46u + 14v = \text{gcd}(46,14).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}46 & = & \color{red}14\cdot 3 & + & \color{red}4 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}14 & = & \color{blue}4\cdot 3 & + & \color{blue}2 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 4 & = & 2 \cdot 2 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(14,46) =2.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}4 &= \color{red} 46 - 14\cdot 3 \\[3pt] \color{blue}2 &= \color{blue} 14 - 4\cdot 3. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 2 &= 14-{\color{red}4}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 14-{\color{red}[46-14\cdot 3]}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 14\cdot 10 - 46\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 46 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-3}) + 14 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{10} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=10.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-3)+10=7. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $90u + 39v = \text{gcd}(90,39).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}90 & = & \color{red}39\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}12 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}39 & = & \color{blue}12\cdot 3 & + & \color{blue}3 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 12 & = & 3 \cdot 4 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(90,39) =3.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}12 &= \color{red} 90 - 39\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}3 &= \color{blue} 39 - 12\cdot 3. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 3 &= 39-{\color{red}12}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 39-{\color{red}[90-39\cdot 2]}\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 39\cdot 7 - 90\cdot 3 \\[3pt] &= 90 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-3}) + 39 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{7} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-3)+7=4. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $70u + 25v = \text{gcd}(70,25).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}70 & = & \color{red}25\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}20 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}25 & = & \color{blue}20\cdot 1 & + & \color{blue}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 20 & = & 5 \cdot 4 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(70,25) =5.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}20 &= \color{red} 70 - 2\cdot 25 \\[3pt] \color{blue}5 &= \color{blue} 25 - 20. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 5 &= 25-{\color{red}20} \\[3pt] &= 25-{\color{red}(70-2\cdot 25)} \\[3pt] &= 25\cdot 3 - 70 \\[3pt] &= 70 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-1}) + 25 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-1$ and $v=3.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-1)+3=2. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $72u + 30v = \text{gcd}(72,30).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}72 & = & \color{red}30\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}12 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}30 & = & \color{blue}12\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}6 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 12 & = & 6 \cdot 2 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(30,72) =6.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}12 &= \color{red} 72 - 30\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}6 &= \color{blue} 30 - 12\cdot 2. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 6 &= 30-{\color{red}12}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 30-{\color{red}[72-30\cdot 2]}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 30\cdot 5 - 72\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 72 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-2}) + 30 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5} \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=-2$ and $v=5.$

Finally, \[u+v=(-2)+5=3. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $53u + 24v = \text{gcd}(53,24).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}53 & = & \color{red}24 \cdot 2 & + & \color{red}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}24 & = & \color{blue}5\cdot 4 & + & \color{blue}4 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 5& = & 4\cdot 1 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(53,24) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}5 &= \color{red} 53 - 24\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}4 &= \color{blue} 24 - 5\cdot 4 \\[3pt] 1 &= 5 - 4. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 5-{\color{blue}4} \\[3pt] &= 5-{\color{blue}(24-5\cdot 4)} \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}5} \cdot 5 - 24 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[53 -24\cdot 2]} \cdot 5 - 24 \\[3pt] &= 53 \cdot 5 - 24 \cdot 11 \\[3pt] &= 53 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5} + 24 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-11}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=5$ and $v=-11.$

Finally, \[u+v=5+(-11)=-6. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $71u + 22v = \text{gcd}(71,22).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}71 & = & \color{red}22\cdot 3 & + & \color{red}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}22& = & \color{blue}5\cdot 4 & + & \color{blue}2 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 5 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(22,71) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}5 &= \color{red} 71 - 22\cdot 3 \\[3pt] \color{blue}2 &= \color{blue} 22 - 5\cdot 4 \\[3pt] 1 &= 5 - 2\cdot 2. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 5-{\color{blue}2}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 5-{\color{blue}[22-5\cdot 4]}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}5}\cdot 9 - 22\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[71-22\cdot 3]}\cdot 9 - 22\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 71\cdot 9 - 22\cdot 29 \\[3pt] &= 71 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{9} + 22 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-29}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-29.$

Finally, \[u+v=9+(-29)=-20. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $47u + 20v = \text{gcd}(47,20).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}47 & = & \color{red}20\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}7 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}20& = & \color{blue}7\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}6 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 7 & = & 6\cdot 1 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(20,47) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}7 &= \color{red} 47 - 20\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}6 &= \color{blue} 20 - 7\cdot 2 \\[3pt] 1 &= 7 - 6. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 7-{\color{blue}6} \\[3pt] &= 7-{\color{blue}(20-7\cdot 2)} \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}7}\cdot 3 - 20 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[47-20\cdot 2]}\cdot 3 - 20 \\[3pt] &= 47\cdot 3 - 20\cdot 7 \\[3pt] &= 47 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3} + 20 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-7}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=3$ and $v=-7.$

Finally, \[u+v=3+(-7)=-4. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $49u + 20v = \text{gcd}(49,20).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}49 & = & \color{red}20\cdot 2 & + & \color{red}9 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}20 & = & \color{blue}9\cdot 2 & + & \color{blue}2 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 9 & = & 2\cdot 4 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(49,20) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}9 &= \color{red} 49 - 20\cdot 2 \\[3pt] \color{blue}2 &= \color{blue} 20 - 9\cdot 2 \\[3pt] 1 &= 9 - 2\cdot 4. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 9-{\color{blue}2}\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= 9-{\color{blue}[20-9\cdot 2]}\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}9}\cdot 9 - 20\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[49-20\cdot 2]}\cdot 9 - 20\cdot 4 \\[3pt] &= 49\cdot 9 - 20\cdot 22\\[4pt] &= 49 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{9} + 20 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-22}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, \[u+v=9+(-22)=-13. \]

question.text: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $59u + 16v = \text{gcd}(59,16).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.explanation:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} \color{red}59 & = & \color{red}16 \cdot 3 & + & \color{red}11 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ \color{blue}16 & = & \color{blue}11\cdot 1 & + & \color{blue}5 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 11 & = & 5\cdot 2 & + & 1 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

As a result, $\text{gcd}(59,16) =1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

\begin{align*} \color{red}11 &= \color{red} 59 - 16\cdot 3 \\[3pt] \color{blue}5 &= \color{blue} 16 - 11 \\[3pt] 1 &= 11 - 5\cdot 2. \end{align*}

Then, we back-substitute:

\begin{align*} 1 &= 11-{\color{blue}5}\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 11-{\color{blue}(16-11)}\cdot2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}11} \cdot 3 - 16\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= {\color{red}[59-16 \cdot 3]} \cdot 3 - 16\cdot 2 \\[3pt] &= 59 \cdot 3 - 16 \cdot 11 \\[3pt] &= 59 \cdot \bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3} + 16 \cdot (\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{-11}) \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Therefore, $u=3$ and $v=-11.$

Finally, \[u+v=3+(-11)=-8. \]
